summary: Full-extraction pass on two Dominica documents: S.R.O. 8 of 2024 (the June 2024 CBI regulations) and the UK written statement HCWS979 imposing visas on Dominica and Vanuatu. The regulations contain only rules and fees (no statistics); all monetary amounts are now recorded as program terms. The statement contains no numbers; one Vanuatu event added.

program_terms.quote: pay a fee of twenty thousand United States dollars before he may file applications with the Unit;
program_terms.notes: Regulations gazetted 28 June 2024. valid_to not given in this document. Payable by 1 January each year, may be prorated for new applications after 1 January.

program_terms.notes: Regulations gazetted 28 June 2024. valid_to not given in this document. The sentence continues on p. 28: "they are allowed to market the Citizenship by Investment Programme to potential clients".

program_terms.notes: Regulations gazetted 28 June 2024. valid_to not given in this document. Plus US$4,000 due diligence on each dependant 16 or older (para 3(2)(b)) and the US$500 certificate fee (para 3(2)(c)). Under S.R.O. 1 of 2024 the fee was US$10,000 (up to 5) or US$15,000 (6 to 17).

Plus US$1,000 processing, US$4,000 due diligence on the spouse, US$7,500 due diligence on the original applicant if submitted more than one year after the original application, and US$1,000 interview (para 3(4)(b)-(e)).

events.title: Increases in CBI contributions kept from pre-agreed project financing
events.description: S.R.O. 8 of 2024 provides that where the Government has agreed to finance a project from CBI contributions or fees and these are increased, the difference is not allocated to the project unless the Minister of Finance approves. The same regulations lower the contribution for an additional adult dependant from US$50,000 to US$40,000 and repeal S.R.O. 1 of 2024.
events.quote: the difference between the original direct monetary investment or fee and the new direct monetary investment or fee shall not be allocated to the project, unless approved by the Minister of Finance.

events.title: UK imposes visa requirement on Vanuatu nationals
events.description: The UK Home Secretary cited abuse of Vanuatu’s (and Dominica’s) CBI scheme, including citizenship granted to people posing a risk to the UK; rules in force 3pm 19 July 2023, transition for existing bookings until 16 August 2023.
events.quote: Careful consideration of Dominica’s and Vanuatu’s operation of a citizenship by investment scheme has shown clear and evident abuse of the scheme

ledger.contains: Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2024 (S.R.O. 8 of 2024, 36 pages, gazetted 28 June 2024, repeals S.R.O. 1 of 2024): definitions (dependants incl. students 18-30 and parents/grandparents over 65), application procedure, mandatory interviews, monthly sharing of denied applicants with CARICOM IMPACS JRCC, denial and deprivation grounds (deprivation after a prison sentence of 12 months or more; no name change for 5 years), real-estate resale (3 years) and reuse (5 years) limits, escrow, notification within three months and proof of title within 30 days, interview committee, enhanced due diligence for specified countries (US$25,000/15,000/15,000/10,000), agents and promoters (eligibility, minimum three staff, bi-annual visits, 10% late penalty), promotional restrictions (fine up to one thousand dollars, currency unspecified; Schedule 2 guidelines), Schedule 1 fees and contributions: direct monetary investment US$200,000 / 250,000 (family of four) / 25,000 and 40,000 per extra dependant; real-estate minimum US$200,000 with government fees US$75,000 / 100,000 / 25,000 / 40,000; due diligence, interview, processing and certificate fees; post-citizenship additions. All amounts recorded as program terms (the US$200,000 contribution, US$200,000 real-estate minimum and US$75,000 government fee were already recorded); the regulations/price event already existed, one rule-change event added for para 1(5). No statistics (applications, approvals, revenue) in the document. Non-monetary periods and procedural rules (3 months, 30 days, 12 months, three staff, 10% penalty, $1,000 fine) are described here, not recorded as terms, following the earlier S.R.O. passes.

UK Home Secretary written statement of 19 July 2023 imposing a visa requirement (and direct airside transit visa) on nationals of Dominica, Honduras, Namibia, Timor-Leste and Vanuatu, citing abuse of Dominica’s and Vanuatu’s CBI schemes; Honduras, Namibia and Timor-Leste reasons concern asylum claims and non-genuine visitors (out of scope). Four-week transition for bookings made before 15:00 BST 19 July 2023 with arrival by 16 August 2023; in force 3pm that day. No programme numbers. Dominica event already existed; added the matching Vanuatu event (vut-cbi) from this statement.
